articleHeadline: African Swine Fever in Vietnam: Innovative biosecurity measures for sustainable pig farming

articleHeadline: Listeria in China: Pregnant women face serious health risks from foodborne bacteria
articleSummary: In Guangdong, China, a pregnant woman was hospitalized after consuming leftover watermelon, leading to a high fever and emergency cesarean delivery. This incident highlights the dangers of Listeria, often referred to as the 'fridge killer,' which can thrive in cold environments and poses significant risks during pregnancy. Symptoms in mothers can be mild, complicating diagnosis. The incubation period for Listeria can range from 3 to 70 days, with an average of 21 days. High-risk foods include unpasteurized dairy, deli meats, and unwashed produce. Pregnant women are advised to report any recent consumption of these foods to healthcare providers to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.
